search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; adaptive candidate streams; measurement validity; lifetime strong FWER; online e-closure versus fallback power

public_sources.title: Family-wise Error Rate Control with E-values
public_sources.used_scope: The latest paper proves post-hoc, anytime and always-valid FWER properties for e-value closed testing in a fixed family, and explicitly distinguishes its fixed-family setting from online closed testing where hypotheses arrive sequentially. Its e-Fallback construction is presented for a fixed ordered sequence H1,...,Hn with pre-specified initial alpha budgets.

public_sources.title: Admissible online closed testing must employ e-values
public_sources.used_scope: Hypotheses H_t may be constructed data-adaptively from past filtration F_{t-1}. Sequential e-values satisfy E[E_t|F_{t-1}]<=1 under true H_t. Products over intersection hypotheses form test supermartingales, and SeqE-Guard gives simultaneous true-discovery lower bounds for adaptive query paths. Fresh independent audit data is a direct route to conditional e-validity even when candidate and e-value design depend on past history.

public_sources.title: The Online Closure Principle
public_sources.authors: Lasse Fischer; Aaditya Ramdas et al.
public_sources.used_scope: Online closure handles a potentially infinite hypothesis stream not fully known in advance and provides strong online FWER control; used as supporting structural context for adaptive candidate identities.

setup: At launch j, candidate/hypothesis H_j must be F_{j-1}-measurable: fully frozen before any fresh audit outcome for j is revealed.
Run a fresh candidate-level anytime e-process and stop it at an F-adapted stopping time tau_j. Emit stopped e-value E_j with E[E_j|F_{j-1}]<=1 under null H_j.
Across the candidate stream, construct Fischer-Ramdas online-closure product intersection e-processes and SeqE-Guard.

For strict commit control, maintain a query set S_t containing committed candidates only. Include a candidate only when doing so raises SeqE-Guard's lower bound d_t by one, and maintain invariant d_t=|S_t|.
adaptive_online_eclosure_commit_gate.guarantee: On the simultaneous SeqE-Guard event, d_t <= number of false nulls in S_t for every t. With d_t=|S_t|, every committed candidate is a false null (a genuine improvement on the tested endpoint). Therefore P(any committed true null ever)<=alpha. This is a lifetime strong-FWER gate despite adaptive candidate identities, adaptive launch times and adaptive within-audit stopping, provided conditional e-validity and candidate freeze hold.
adaptive_online_eclosure_commit_gate.scope_guard: This does not repair a candidate test whose validation data were reused during candidate construction in a way that breaks E[E_j|F_{j-1}]<=1. Fresh audit or an explicitly valid conditional-data-reuse construction remains required.

hartog_lei_scope_boundary.finding: Hartog-Lei v4 explicitly states that its setting has a fixed set of hypotheses and differs from online closed testing where hypotheses arrive sequentially. Its fixed-family e-Fallback recurrence should not be cited as direct proof for adaptively generated hypothesis identities without a separate online proof.
hartog_lei_scope_boundary.consequence: Use Fischer-Ramdas online closure/SeqE-Guard as the currently justified adaptive-identity interface; keep Hartog-Lei e-Fallback as a fixed-family reference and possible future recurrence to re-prove online.

delayed_signal_collapse_condition.mechanism: For strict singleton-style certification under product online e-closure, prior off-query noncommitted e-values below one can accumulate a multiplicative penalty C_{t-1}=prod_{j<t,uncommitted} min(E_j,1), making a later candidate need evidence roughly E_t >= 1/(alpha*C_{t-1}).
delayed_signal_collapse_condition.typical_behavior: If null emitted e-values are nondegenerate and E[log min(E_j,1)]<0, or a suitable uniformly negative conditional-drift analogue holds, log C_t typically decreases linearly and the later evidence threshold grows exponentially.
delayed_signal_collapse_condition.scope_guard: This is a simple explanatory condition for the tested/stylized process, not a theorem for arbitrary dependent adaptive e-value streams without additional drift assumptions.

worker_local_stress_tests.model: Fresh paired binary audits. Each task is concordant with probability 0.6; among discordant pairs q_null=0.5 and q_good=0.75. Fixed sign e-factor for q_bet=0.75: candidate-only factor 1.5, incumbent-only factor 0.5, concordant factor 1. Global alpha=0.05. Results are worker-local Monte Carlo, not deployment guarantees.

clustered_markov_stream_30000_runs.proposal_process: 30 proposal opportunities, max 20 audits; two-state hot/cold Markov quality regime with P(hot|hot)=0.85, P(hot|cold)=0.15, P(good|hot)=0.65, P(good|cold)=0.10; development triage launches 0.80 of good and 0.25 of null candidates; max 50 fresh paired tasks per audit.
clustered_markov_stream_30000_runs.interpretation: In this early/clustered-signal regime, product online e-closure used more of the global risk budget and produced more true commits with fewer fresh tasks while remaining below nominal alpha in simulation.

deterministic_timing_50000_runs.interpretation: Product online e-closure is excellent for strong alternatives arriving early/clustered, but can catastrophically lose late-stream resolution because past noncommitted null e-values below one multiply an exponentially worsening certification penalty. Geometric fallback is substantially more robust to delayed or sparse improvements in the tested horizon.

simple_hedging.tested: Replace base one-step factor by 1+h*(base-1) for h in {0.75,0.5}.
simple_hedging.result: h=0.75 reduced null crossing but did not remove delayed-signal collapse. h=0.5 largely destroyed 50-task alpha-spending/fallback power and still did not rescue late product-closure performance.
simple_hedging.conclusion: Naive hedge-to-one is not a sufficient fix.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Adaptive candidate identities H_t are F_{t-1}-measurable; emit conditionally valid stopped fresh e-values; use Fischer-Ramdas online product closure and SeqE-Guard; commit only when the lower bound increments so d_t remains equal to the number of committed candidates.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Direct mapping to Fischer-Ramdas v4 plus the invariant argument above.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Requires candidate freeze and conditional fresh-null e-validity for every launched audit.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Treat Hartog-Lei e-Fallback as fixed-family/fixed-sequence evidence only until an adaptive-online proof is supplied.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Latest v4 explicitly contrasts its fixed set with online closed testing.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Off-query e-values below one accumulate multiplicatively and can make later singleton certification exponentially harder.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Worker-local all-null/delayed/early signal stress plus negative truncated-log-drift explanation.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Power pathology, not a Type-I-validity failure.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Precommit a valid risk/evidence portfolio combining an early-signal-sensitive online-closure route with a delayed-signal-robust fallback/spending route, or boost/truncate sequential e-values inside SeqE-Guard, rather than selecting the stronger procedure after seeing the same audit evidence.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected: 'Hartog-Lei e-Fallback already proves strong FWER for adaptively generated candidate identities.' The latest paper explicitly studies a fixed family and points to separate online-closure work for sequentially arriving hypotheses.

Rejected: 'adaptive candidate identities make strong lifetime FWER impossible.' Fischer-Ramdas permits H_t to be F_{t-1}-measurable; conditional e-values plus online closure/SeqE-Guard give a direct strong-FWER interface.

Rejected: 'a stronger exact online closure is operationally uniformly better than alpha spending/fallback.' The tested product closure can lose essentially all late-signal power after repeated null/noncommit evidence.
Narrowed: 'hedging each e-factor toward one fixes late-signal collapse.' Simple h=0.75/0.5 hedging did not solve the tested pathology.
Narrowed: 'the product penalty decay theorem holds for arbitrary adaptive dependence.' The negative-log-drift explanation needs explicit stochastic conditions.

frontier.action: Study Fischer-Ramdas sequential-e-value boosting/truncation specifically for fresh paired-sign audits. Derive whether bounded lower-tail damage can reduce off-query penalty collapse while preserving conditional e-validity and lifetime adaptive-identity FWER; stress-test delayed, sparse and clustered improvements.

Attempt a separate online conditional proof for the prefix-style Hartog-Lei e-Fallback recurrence with adaptively generated H_t and conditionally valid E_t. Do not adopt it unless the proof closes; compare its late-signal behavior with geometric p-fallback and product closure.

Derive a safe fixed-risk hybrid/portfolio between product online closure and fallback/spending. Avoid data-dependent cherry-picking between procedures unless the combination itself has a proven FWER/e-value guarantee.

Retain the prior lifetime/epoch and multiple-endpoint frontier: model-version or benchmark refresh must not silently reset alpha, and catastrophic-regression endpoints need separate protection from average-improvement endpoints.

exact_next_action: Read and derive the sequential-e-value boosting/truncation construction in Fischer-Ramdas for the paired-sign fresh-audit process, then simulate boosted SeqE-Guard versus geometric fallback across delayed/clustered regimes while verifying conditional null e-validity and lifetime strong FWER.
